TASK.md: Django issue #13033 — `order_by()` on a self-referencing FK's `_id` field produced an unexpected `DESC` sort and an unnecessary extra join. Fix the cause in source, no test changes, no commit.

## Root cause
In `find_ordering_name` (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:730`), the guard

```python
if field.is_relation and opts.ordering and getattr(field, 'attname', None) != name and name != 'pk':
```

compares the FK's `attname` (`root_id`) against `name` — the **entire dotted path** (`record__root_id`). For any multi-part path the two never match, so Django treats `record__root_id` as ordering by the relation itself: it appends `OneModel.Meta.ordering` (`-id` → the unexpected `DESC`) and returns early, skipping `query.trim_joins(...)` — which is why the extra `LEFT OUTER JOIN T3` survives. A single-part `order_by("root_id")` worked only because the path happened to equal the attname.

## Fix (one line, source only)
```diff
-        if field.is_relation and opts.ordering and getattr(field, 'attname', None) != name and name != 'pk':
+        if field.is_relation and opts.ordering and getattr(field, 'attname', None) != pieces[-1] and name != 'pk':
```
`pieces[-1]` is the last path component — the attribute name actually specified — so `record__root_id` is now recognized as the attname shortcut. (This mirrors how upstream Django later fixed this exact issue.)
